rubric.why: The law applies only within the elastic limit.
rubric.description: States the condition under which Hooke’s law applies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the elastic limit.

rubric.why: The defining relationship is that the extension or compression varies directly with the applied force.
rubric.description: States the proportional relationship between extension or compression and applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expressing that extension or compression is directly proportional to force.

modelAnswer: If a force F is applied on a spring to stretch or compress it, the extension or compression x has been found directly proportional to the applied force within the elastic limit.

rubric.why: Mass is the quantity used in the definition of density.
rubric.description: Identifies mass as the quantity being measured per unit volume.

rubric.why: Density is mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: States that the mass is measured per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning unit volume.

modelAnswer: Density of a substance is defined as its mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: Pressure is defined using a force acting normally on a surface.
rubric.description: Identifies the force as acting normally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning force acting normally.

rubric.why: Pressure is force per unit area.
rubric.description: States that the force acts on unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning unit area.

modelAnswer: Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on unit area of an object.

rubric.why: Pascal’s law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.description: States that pressure is applied at a point in an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning applied pressure and an enclosed fluid.

rubric.why: The applied pressure is transmitted equally throughout the fluid without loss.
rubric.description: States that pressure is transmitted equally to all parts of the fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning equal transmission to all parts.

modelAnswer: When pressure is applied at one point in an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted equally to all parts of fluid without loss.

rubric.why: Pebbles reduce the area over which the reaction force acts.
rubric.description: States that the contact area is reduced when walking on pebbles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning reduced contact area.

rubric.why: The reduced contact area produces high pressure, making walking painful.
rubric.description: Links the high pressure due to the reaction force with the pain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the high pressure causes pain.

modelAnswer: But when we walk on pebbles, the contact area is reduced. Then the pressure due to reaction force becomes so high that it becomes painful.

rubric.why: Liquid pressure increases as depth increases.
rubric.description: States that pressure in a liquid increases with depth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that pressure increases with depth.

rubric.why: The pressure value depends on both the depth and the liquid’s density.
rubric.description: States that liquid pressure depends on depth and density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning both depth and density.

modelAnswer: Equation 6.4 shows that pressure in a liquid increases with depth. The value of pressure depends on the depth and density of the liquid.
